**Entry 2 – First Annual General Meeting, 1975**

Date of record: 1975-03-20
Initialled: JPH

The first AGM was held at the Swan Inn, Marlow. The Chairman reported that membership had grown from 15 to 32 during the first season. The Club had acquired a second boat, a double scull, donated by a retiring member of the Marlow Amateur Rowing Club (see donation letter, ref. DON/75/002).

The accounts for the year ending 31 December 1974 were presented and adopted. Income: £214 (subscriptions) + £45 (donations) = £259. Expenditure: £132 (boat repairs) + £38 (insurance) + £22 (stationery and postage) = £192. Balance carried forward: £67.

It was agreed that the Club would seek affiliation with the Amateur Rowing Association (ARA) during the coming year. This was completed in October 1975 (certificate on file, ref. AFF/75/001).

**Entry 3 – Proposed Club Extension, 1976 (Not Pursued)**

Date of record: 1976-09-02
Initialled: JPH

At a committee meeting held on 2 September 1976, a proposal was discussed to extend the boat shed by an additional 30 feet to provide covered storage for up to four additional boats and a small workshop area. The proposal was put forward by the then Captain, R. T. Ingram, who had prepared sketch plans and a rough cost estimate of £850.

The committee considered the proposal over two further meetings. Concerns were raised regarding (a) the availability of funds, (b) the need to obtain planning permission from Wycombe District Council, and (c) the possibility that the Club might relocate to a larger site within a few years.
**Riverside Rowing Club Administrative Records**

Three candidates were interviewed on 12 August 2021. The appointment was offered to Claire Ashworth, of Marlow, who had previously worked as an administrative assistant at a local veterinary practice and had been a member of the Club since 2018.

**Entry 31 – Minutes of the June Committee Meeting (Excerpts)**

Date of record: 2025-06-12
Initialled: AP

The June committee meeting was held on 11 June in the clubhouse lounge, with six of the seven committee members present. The Boathouse Manager was in attendance for the equipment items. The following items were discussed and decisions recorded.

1. **Buoyancy aids (item from DR-2025-014).** The request for 6 new buoyancy aids was approved, subject to the usual supplier being able to deliver before the start of the summer learn-to-row sessions. KL confirmed that the 3 unfit aids have been removed from the racks and will be disposed of once the new stock arrives. The 6 with minor wear will be kept as spares and rotated out as they deteriorate. KL to raise PO-2025-043.

2. **Summer rowing camp.** The junior squad coordinator's proposal for a week-long camp (21–25 July) was discussed at length. The main concerns were coach availability and the impact on the senior squad's training schedule, as both groups share the same water time in the mornings. The coordinator confirmed that two volunteer coaches have already been lined up and that the camp would run in the afternoons only, which would avoid a clash. The committee agreed in principle to proceed, with the final go-ahead subject to the completion of a risk assessment and confirmation of the volunteer coaches' safeguarding checks. AP to circulate the draft risk assessment by 20 June.

3. **Equipment budget.** The Boathouse Manager reported that the oar order (PO-2025-041) is still with the supplier and is expected to arrive in early July. In the meantime, the squad will continue to use the spare oars. The manager also noted that the cost of the buoyancy aids was within the approved budget line, and no further authorisation was required.

4. **Social event proposal.** A proposal for a club barbecue and family fun day in August was tabled by the social secretary. The committee was broadly supportive, but a minority view was expressed that the event should be held later in the month to avoid clashing with the summer camp and the annual regatta. After discussion, it was agreed that the social secretary would check the regatta date and confirm the event date by the end of June. No final decision was taken.

5. **Membership update.** The membership secretary reported that the club had 214 members as of the end of May, up from 198 at the same point last year. The junior squad has a waiting list of 12, and the learn-to-row programme is fully booked for the summer. The committee noted this with satisfaction.

---

**Entry 32 – Risk Assessment Draft – Summer Rowing Camp**

Date of record: 2025-06-18
Initialled: AP

A draft risk assessment for the summer rowing camp has been prepared and circulated to the committee and the junior squad coordinator. The assessment covers the usual items: water safety, weather, equipment checks, and supervision ratios. The key points are summarised below.

- **Water safety.** All sessions will be led by a qualified coach with a rescue boat on the water at all times. The club's safety boat will be checked before each session.
- **Weather.** Sessions will be cancelled or moved indoors if the wind speed exceeds the club's normal threshold or if there is a thunderstorm warning. The decision will be made by the coach on the day.
- **Equipment.** All boats and oars used by the camp will be checked before the first session. The camp will use the club's training boats, which are in good condition. The damaged oar noted in the equipment log will not be used; the new order is expected to arrive before the camp begins.
- **Supervision.** The ratio will be one coach per six juniors, with at least two volunteers on the bank. All volunteers must have completed a safeguarding check before the camp starts.

Riverside Rowing Club established_year 1974 year. Record status: current. The Club was formally constituted at a public meeting held at the Old Boathouse, Marlow, on 14 June 1974, following two years of informal rowing activity by a group of local enthusiasts. The constitution was adopted unanimously, and the first officers were elected as set out in the minutes of that meeting (held on file, ref. CONST/74/001).

---

**Entry 2 – First Annual General Meeting, 1975**

Date of record: 1975-03-20
Initialled: JPH

The first AGM was held at the Swan Inn, Marlow. The Chairman reported that membership had grown from 15 to 32 during the first season. The Club had acquired a second boat, a double scull, donated by a retiring member of the Marlow Amateur Rowing Club (see donation letter, ref. DON/75/002).

The accounts for the year ending 31 December 1974 were presented and adopted. Income: £214 (subscriptions) + £45 (donations) = £259. Expenditure: £132 (boat repairs) + £38 (insurance) + £22 (stationery and postage) = £192. Balance carried forward: £67.

It was agreed that the Club would seek affiliation with the Amateur Rowing Association (ARA) during the coming year. This was completed in October 1975 (certificate on file, ref. AFF/75/001).

---

**Entry 3 – Proposed Club Extension, 1976 (Not Pursued)**

Date of record: 1976-09-02
Initialled: JPH

At a committee meeting held on 2 September 1976, a proposal was discussed to extend the boat shed by an additional 30 feet to provide covered storage for up to four additional boats and a small workshop area. The proposal was put forward by the then Captain, R. T. Ingram, who had prepared sketch plans and a rough cost estimate of £850.

The committee considered the proposal over two further meetings. Concerns were raised regarding (a) the availability of funds, (b) the need to obtain planning permission from Wycombe District Council, and (c) the possibility that the Club might relocate to a larger site within a few years.

- Use of ergometers for junior training
- Correcting common technique faults
- Designing circuit sessions for small groups

**Entry 31 – Minutes of the June Committee Meeting (Excerpts)**

Date of record: 2025-06-12
Initialled: AP

The June committee meeting was held on 11 June in the clubhouse lounge, with six of the seven committee members present. The Boathouse Manager was in attendance for the equipment items. The following items were discussed and decisions recorded.

1. **Buoyancy aids (item from DR-2025-014).** The request for 6 new buoyancy aids was approved, subject to the usual supplier being able to deliver before the start of the summer learn-to-row sessions. KL confirmed that the 3 unfit aids have been removed from the racks and will be disposed of once the new stock arrives. The 6 with minor wear will be kept as spares and rotated out as they deteriorate. KL to raise PO-2025-043.

2. **Summer rowing camp.** The junior squad coordinator's proposal for a week-long camp (21–25 July) was discussed at length. The main concerns were coach availability and the impact on the senior squad's training schedule, as both groups share the same water time in the mornings. The coordinator confirmed that two volunteer coaches have already been lined up and that the camp would run in the afternoons only, which would avoid a clash. The committee agreed in principle to proceed, with the final go-ahead subject to the completion of a risk assessment and confirmation of the volunteer coaches' safeguarding checks. AP to circulate the draft risk assessment by 20 June.

3. **Equipment budget.** The Boathouse Manager reported that the oar order (PO-2025-041) is still with the supplier and is expected to arrive in early July. In the meantime, the squad will continue to use the spare oars. The manager also noted that the cost of the buoyancy aids was within the approved budget line, and no further authorisation was required.

4. **Social event proposal.** A proposal for a club barbecue and family fun day in August was tabled by the social secretary. The committee was broadly supportive, but a minority view was expressed that the event should be held later in the month to avoid clashing with the summer camp and the annual regatta. After discussion, it was agreed that the social secretary would check the regatta date and confirm the event date by the end of June. No final decision was taken.

5. **Membership update.** The membership secretary reported that the club had 214 members as of the end of May, up from 198 at the same point last year. The junior squad has a waiting list of 12, and the learn-to-row programme is fully booked for the summer. The committee noted this with satisfaction.

---

**Entry 32 – Risk Assessment Draft – Summer Rowing Camp**

Date of record: 2025-06-18
Initialled: AP

A draft risk assessment for the summer rowing camp has been prepared and circulated to the committee and the junior squad coordinator. The assessment covers the usual items: water safety, weather, equipment checks, and supervision ratios. The key points are summarised below.

- **Water safety.** All sessions will be led by a qualified coach with a rescue boat on the water at all times. The club's safety boat will be checked before each session.
- **Weather.** Sessions will be cancelled or moved indoors if the wind speed exceeds the club's normal threshold or if there is a thunderstorm warning. The decision will be made by the coach on the day.
- **Equipment.** All boats and oars used by the camp will be checked before the first session. The camp will use the club's training boats, which are in good condition. The damaged oar noted in the equipment log will not be used; the new order is expected to arrive before the camp begins.
- **Supervision.** The ratio will be one coach per six juniors, with at least two volunteers on the bank. All volunteers must have completed a safeguarding check before the camp starts.
